I have a classmate who is really interested in guns, knives, explosives etc., we'll call him a. many weeks back, i took back some magnesium powder from the school lab for campfire effects.
A saw me placing it inside my locker, and offered to trade a spoonful of magnesium for a handmade firecracker explosive.
I agreed, as it sounded pretty awesome.
It looked like a cherry bomb but it was really small.
He told me that all i had to do was to light up the fuse and wait for it to explode.
Today i attempted to detonate it in class.
That was the first mistake because its an enclosed classroom.
Everyone else was at other lessons so it was empty.
Moving the tables to the side, i created a space where it could "safely detonate".
Lighting it, i ran to the back of class and took cover.
The fuse was a sparkler and it burnt all the way till the flash powder, but nothing happened.
I took out the fuse and realized that the portion of it inside the flash powder had already disintegrated.
This is the stupid part.
I didn't know what i was thinking.
Maybe i thought it was a dud or something.
I took my lighter and lit the rest of it.
My left hand (thumb, index and middle finger) was holding it when it exploded.
It was really loud and made me go partially deaf for the next 5 minutes.
My fingertips are heavily bruised and there is a bit of internal bleeding under my middle fingernail.
Right now i'm suffering from tinnitus in my left ear as i type with only my right hand.
My left hand is in a sock with ointment on it.
My only fear of this is that my hearing may be damaged and this could result in me not being able to go for a private pilot license course i plan to take up at the end of the year.
If anyone has shot guns without earplugs before, you may know what i'm going through now.
Do advise.
I didn't dare to tell my parents the truth, so i told them i smashed my fingers in the doorway.
For the hearing issue, i'm not sure how i'm gonna explain that.
P.s i think this is karma, because i drew a huge realistic penis on my friend's physics workbook yesterday.
Doesn't help that the 3 fingers injured form fleming's left hand rule.
Update: fingers and hearing pretty much back to normal, now i've paid the price of stupidity.
Now i think through everything many times before making a decision to avoid future fus.
Have a nice day.

One of the longest-held detainees at the us facility at guantanamo bay, a kuwaiti man, has been sent home, officials say.
Fawzi al-odah, 37, was released after a us review panel concluded he was not a "continuing significant threat".
He had been at the us facility in cuba since 2002 after his arrest in pakistan on suspicion of links to al-qaeda and the taliban - a charge he denies.
He had challenged america's right to detain him in the us supreme court.
Mr odah boarded a kuwaiti government plane on wednesday morning us time.
"there's no bitterness, there's no anger," his lawyer eric lewis was quoted as saying by the associated press news agency.
"there's just excitement and joy that he will be going home."
The release came after guantanamo's periodic review board in july determined "that continued law of war detention of (mr odah) does not remain necessary to protect against a continuing significant threat to the security of the united states".
But he now faces at least a year at a militant rehabilitation centre in kuwait, according to the terms of the release.
The kuwaiti government had pushed hard for the release of all kuwaiti detainees at guantanamo.
Mr odah had argued that he travelled to afghanistan and pakistan to teach the koran and provide humanitarian aid.
He is the first inmate to be freed since may, when five taliban detainees were exchanged for us sgt bowe bergdahl, who had been kept by the insurgents in afghanistan.
Mr odah's release brings down the total number of inmates at the us naval base to 148.
The us opened the facility in january 2002, following the 11 september 2001 attacks in america.
President barack obama has repeatedly promised to shut it down.

His release comes after a review panel determined that his detention was no longer necessary and brings the total number of inmates at Guantanamo Bay down to 148.

This happened in the past.
My co-workers and i decided to go out for some beers and thursday night karaoke at a nearby bar on a hot september evening.
Every one was having a good time, drinking beers, eating pizza and getting loud.
A song had been stuck in my head for days and by god i was going to get it out through the power of karaoke.
I submitted my song to the dj and waited patiently through some truly horrendous versions of the b-52s, journey and the usual karaoke suspects.
Finally my name was called, and after several bars of power chords, i began to sing a pitch perfect version of rock you like a hurricane by the scorpions.
I was nailing it; i mean i was on fire and i was feeling it but when i looked out into the audience there was nothing but shaking heads and even some looks of anger.
What the hell was going on i thought.
And suddenly just as the second verse started i realized what i'd done.
You see the date of this thursday karaoke night was sept. 1, 2005, and the reason that song was stuck in my head was that hurricane katrina had been in the news all week.
I never even associated the two things, but the audience clearly thought i was trying to make a mockery of the event.
Why hadn't my friends stopped me?
Maybe they were drunk.
Why hadn't the karaoke dj stopped me?
Maybe he thought i deserved the ass kicking that i was clearly asking for.
I weakly finished the song, dropped some cash on the table, and slunk out the door never to return.

The narrator sings Rock You Like a Hurricane by the Scorpions, unaware that the audience perceives it as mocking the disaster. Despite the audience's negative reaction, they finish the song and leave the bar.

Both me and my girlfriend participate in winter sports at our highschool, i swim and she fences.
Today was a late meet for me (8pm meet) and it is a rule we must dress up for a meet.
My girlfriend has a normal practice today, normally school gets out at 3:02 and her practice is at 3:15. she has to get changed so i wait outside the locker rooms for her so i could give her a kiss goodbye.
What i don't realize is that my bus leaves while i'm standing outside the locker rooms.
Being a slow dresser she is in there till the last minute.
After she comes out i give her a kiss goodbye and walk outside.
There was nothing, nobody, but the steady snow fall.
Naturally i freak out and start making calls, my friend says he got dropped off already so i call my house... no answer.. my parents and older sister are working so no answer from them.. now i'm paying the price with a 6 mile walk hold in freezing temperatures in my thin dress shirt and no gloves or hat.
Wish me luck!
!

What i don't realize is that my bus leaves while i'm standing outside the locker rooms.
Being a slow dresser she is in there till the last minute.
After she comes out i give her a kiss goodbye and walk outside.
There was nothing, nobody, but the steady snow fall.
Naturally i freak out and start making calls, my friend says he got dropped off already so i call my house... no answer.. my parents and older sister are working so no answer from them.. now i'm paying the price with a 6 mile walk hold in freezing temperatures in my thin dress shirt and no gloves or hat.
Wish me luck!

This was about a week or two ago but i still think i should share this with you guys.
I was at football practice.
It was the first day of spring practice and i was practicing for qb (quarterbacks throw the ball for people who don't keep up with sports).
I practiced the whole day, got dehydrated and ended up almost passing out.
I asked a coach to go get water but he told me to continue to do the rest of the sprints.
Anyways, it became the end of the day.
It was time for me to practice with the whole offense.
I got in the huddle, called "flex right 2" and the just said "break?
".
For people who don't know, that's not how you do a huddle, this is how you do a huddle: 1) make sure your center is looking at you; make sure your huddle is worth something 2) make sure all eyes are on you 3) say the play twice on both sides of the huddle 4) say "ready, break" i figured it out and i got in position.
I said, "ready go" and the center snapped me the ball.
Now listen, i have no idea what i just called in the huddle.
I just copied exactly what coach told me to say but i didn't know what "flex right 2" was.
So, i got the snap, i looked to my right, and threw the ball to the right outside wide receiver.
I was so proud of myself.
"i threw an accurate pass to the wr and coach will be proud!!"
I thought.
Then the offensive line gets up and says, "didn't he say two?"
I thought, "yeah i said two?"
So i get back in the huddle, and i asked coach, "did i do something wrong?"
"hell yeah!"
He yelled, "you threw on a run play!"
Instantly, i thought i was going to get kicked off the team.
The only thing i could do was say, "i'm so sorry," about 30 times.
I ended up getting yelled at, told if i do that again, i was being moved to another position, and i got laughed at and made fun of for the rest of the week and still even today by other players and friends.
So i quit.
I talked to my coach about it and since he knows i want to play guitar and film more, he offered a shot to go back during the fall and actually film the games!
Then he said if i want to make a career out of it, he could call his good friend from south carolina to possibly get me scholarship money to go down there and film the games.

Later, during a huddle, the author accidentally called the wrong play, leading to confusion and criticism from the coach and teammates. The author eventually quit the team and shifted focus to their passion for guitar and filmmaking, receiving an opportunity to film the games during the fall and possibly even secure a scholarship for filming at a college in South Carolina.

Context: i've recently come down with a pretty nasty ear infection, that just seems to get worse.
On the first day, my inner ear felt congested, and flared up in pain when i bit down on anything.
Obviously, i decide to head to a clinic, and was promptly diagnosed with an inner ear infection.
On the second day, i felt lightheaded and dizzy, but decided to push on through.
However, by the third day, i was starting to feel queasy, and heavily feverish.
I checked my temp with an oral thermometer, and, just as i suspected, i was running a low fever.
Now, here's where the tifu starts.
A couple weeks back, i made plans with a friend to go see justice league.
We were both pretty hyped up, because we're pretty big fans of the characters.
Even though i was feeling pretty shitty, i decided to go through with our  plans, and go anyways.
I had started to feel a little better by the time noon rolled around, so i thought i could keep it together until i got back home.
Boy, was i wrong.
When we got to the theater, my fever had slowly started to return, along with a stomach ache.
It started out pretty mild, but slowly progressed.
By the midway point, i was barely keeping it together.
Around the setup to the climax, i could feel my throat burning, and my stomach rumbling like a geyser, preparing to erupt.
And erupt it did... as i was starting to get ready to make a break for the bathroom, the inevitable time bomb that was my gut finally exploded.
Thanks to the advice i'd gotten about staying hydrated, the nearly-endless stream of vomit that shot out of my mouth was extra liquidy, leading to an ever growing puddle of puke, swelling up around my shoes.
Quickly, the soupy stream of spew made it's way down the isle, alerting everyone that hadn't already noticed the atrocity i had just committed before them.
Soon came an endless torrent of remarks, such as "geez, why's it all wet here?
", "who just spilled their drink?"
"why is my shoe so moist?"
And many more.
Eventually, the ushers had become aware of the mess i had  just jettisoned from my throat, and started evacuating the theater.
I couldn't make eye contact with my friend, as i rushed back to my car to speed home.

I work in a secure mental health hospital in the uk.
I typically work night shifts and last night i was getting peckish.
I thought to myself i'll pop some toast in and quickly go do my observations, by the time i'm back it will be ready.
As i'm doing my checks a couple of patients asked me to do some little things for them and i assist them, completely forgetting about my toast.
Next thing i know, the fire alarms are ringing.
See the interesting thing about secure door locks is that they become unlocked in the event of a fire, to allow people to get out the building, and well, the interesting thing about secure hospitals is that they are supposed to be locked... for the briefest of moments i was confused, then suddenly it dawned on me.
Toast.
I ran to the staff room (which, previously only accessible by staff,  was now open to all as the internal locks are released too) and found smoke billowing from the toaster and a patient sat next to it laughing and munching his way through the black charcoal blocks that remained of my snack.
Luckily, we managed to secure the building, reset the alarm and escort the patient back to his room with no harm done.
One patient however did manage to get out the building however and had to be picked up by police later in the night.
Lesson to self, no more toast on night shift.
Safe to say my manager was not impressed.
summary: On a secure mental health hospital night shift, an employee forgot about their toast, leading to an unexpected fire alarm and evacuation. Although no harm was done, it served as a lesson to the employee to not be distracted by personal matters while on the job.

Toast.

One patient however did manage to get out the building however and had to be picked up by police later in the night.
Lesson to self, no more toast on night shift.
Safe to say my manager was not impressed.
summary: On a secure mental health hospital night shift, an employee forgot about their toast, leading to an unexpected fire alarm and evacuation. Although no harm was done, it served as a lesson to the employee to not be distracted by personal matters while on the job.

I work in a secure mental health hospital in the uk.
I typically work night shifts and last night i was getting peckish.
I thought to myself i'll pop some toast in and quickly go do my observations, by the time i'm back it will be ready.
As i'm doing my checks a couple of patients asked me to do some little things for them and i assist them, completely forgetting about my toast.
Next thing i know, the fire alarms are ringing.
See the interesting thing about secure door locks is that they become unlocked in the event of a fire, to allow people to get out the building, and well, the interesting thing about secure hospitals is that they are supposed to be locked... for the briefest of moments i was confused, then suddenly it dawned on me.
Toast.
I ran to the staff room (which, previously only accessible by staff,  was now open to all as the internal locks are released too) and found smoke billowing from the toaster and a patient sat next to it laughing and munching his way through the black charcoal blocks that remained of my snack.
Luckily, we managed to secure the building, reset the alarm and escort the patient back to his room with no harm done.
One patient however did manage to get out the building however and had to be picked up by police later in the night.
Lesson to self, no more toast on night shift.
Safe to say my manager was not impressed.

I have a classmate who is really interested in guns, knives, explosives etc., we'll call him a. many weeks back, i took back some magnesium powder from the school lab for campfire effects.
A saw me placing it inside my locker, and offered to trade a spoonful of magnesium for a handmade firecracker explosive.
I agreed, as it sounded pretty awesome.
It looked like a cherry bomb but it was really small.
He told me that all i had to do was to light up the fuse and wait for it to explode.
Today i attempted to detonate it in class.
That was the first mistake because its an enclosed classroom.
Everyone else was at other lessons so it was empty.
Moving the tables to the side, i created a space where it could "safely detonate".
Lighting it, i ran to the back of class and took cover.
The fuse was a sparkler and it burnt all the way till the flash powder, but nothing happened.
I took out the fuse and realized that the portion of it inside the flash powder had already disintegrated.
This is the stupid part.
I didn't know what i was thinking.
Maybe i thought it was a dud or something.
I took my lighter and lit the rest of it.
My left hand (thumb, index and middle finger) was holding it when it exploded.
It was really loud and made me go partially deaf for the next 5 minutes.
My fingertips are heavily bruised and there is a bit of internal bleeding under my middle fingernail.
Right now i'm suffering from tinnitus in my left ear as i type with only my right hand.
My left hand is in a sock with ointment on it.
My only fear of this is that my hearing may be damaged and this could result in me not being able to go for a private pilot license course i plan to take up at the end of the year.
If anyone has shot guns without earplugs before, you may know what i'm going through now.
Do advise.
I didn't dare to tell my parents the truth, so i told them i smashed my fingers in the doorway.
For the hearing issue, i'm not sure how i'm gonna explain that.
P.s i think this is karma, because i drew a huge realistic penis on my friend's physics workbook yesterday.
Doesn't help that the 3 fingers injured form fleming's left hand rule.
Update: fingers and hearing pretty much back to normal, now i've paid the price of stupidity.
Now i think through everything many times before making a decision to avoid future fus.
Have a nice day.

This happened in the past.
My co-workers and i decided to go out for some beers and thursday night karaoke at a nearby bar on a hot september evening.
Every one was having a good time, drinking beers, eating pizza and getting loud.
A song had been stuck in my head for days and by god i was going to get it out through the power of karaoke.
I submitted my song to the dj and waited patiently through some truly horrendous versions of the b-52s, journey and the usual karaoke suspects.
Finally my name was called, and after several bars of power chords, i began to sing a pitch perfect version of rock you like a hurricane by the scorpions.
I was nailing it; i mean i was on fire and i was feeling it but when i looked out into the audience there was nothing but shaking heads and even some looks of anger.
What the hell was going on i thought.
And suddenly just as the second verse started i realized what i'd done.
You see the date of this thursday karaoke night was sept. 1, 2005, and the reason that song was stuck in my head was that hurricane katrina had been in the news all week.
I never even associated the two things, but the audience clearly thought i was trying to make a mockery of the event.
Why hadn't my friends stopped me?
Maybe they were drunk.
Why hadn't the karaoke dj stopped me?
Maybe he thought i deserved the ass kicking that i was clearly asking for.
I weakly finished the song, dropped some cash on the table, and slunk out the door never to return.

This happened a week or two ago.
I was in scotland with the main intention of climbing ben nevis, the highest mountain in the uk.
I woke up pretty early for this, and when i woke up realised my toenails needed cutting first.
But i was too tired, and the process of breakfast made me forget, and me and my dad set off.
There was little problem on the ascent, although i did realise that i'd forgotten about halfway up.
The walk down, however, was different.
After ten minutes of descent, with all of me feeling like shit from the climb, my big toe began to hurt.
Eventually it got to the point where i had to take baby steps to minimise the pain.
By the last half of the mountain every tiny step felt like i was stunning my toe.
Normally it's quicker when you go down a mountain compared to the climb, but my memory cost me hours and a shit ton of pain, by the end my legs were shaking and stiff, as i had to keep myself from moving too far with each step, using far more energy than i would have otherwise.
I felt sick and, after sitting down at the bottom, could barely bring myself to limp to the car park, since then the nail on my big toe has gone black, but the pain is gone.
summary: when climbing ben nevis, even though the climb itself wasn't too difficult, it was difficult to descend due to pain in the feet.

Yesterday while she was out on an errand i snuck out and bought a very expensive cartier item, making it back home before she got back.
This morning she wakes me up and shows me her phone with a worried look on her face.
On it there's a message from her bank warning her that a very large purchase was made on her credit card.
I jump out of bed, yelling "what the fuck!"
And grab my wallet, finding inside my wife's, identical to my own, credit card rather than my card.
The night before we went to dinner and must have switched our cards after paying.
Kinda shocked that cartier didn't bother to check the name on the card as we have completely different names.

This happened a week or two ago.
I was in scotland with the main intention of climbing ben nevis, the highest mountain in the uk.
I woke up pretty early for this, and when i woke up realised my toenails needed cutting first.
But i was too tired, and the process of breakfast made me forget, and me and my dad set off.
There was little problem on the ascent, although i did realise that i'd forgotten about halfway up.
The walk down, however, was different.
After ten minutes of descent, with all of me feeling like shit from the climb, my big toe began to hurt.
Eventually it got to the point where i had to take baby steps to minimise the pain.
By the last half of the mountain every tiny step felt like i was stunning my toe.
Normally it's quicker when you go down a mountain compared to the climb, but my memory cost me hours and a shit ton of pain, by the end my legs were shaking and stiff, as i had to keep myself from moving too far with each step, using far more energy than i would have otherwise.
I felt sick and, after sitting down at the bottom, could barely bring myself to limp to the car park, since then the nail on my big toe has gone black, but the pain is gone.
summary: The author went on a trip to Scotland with the intention of climbing Ben Nevis, the highest mountain in the UK. They woke up early but forgot to cut their toenails before setting off with their dad. During the descent, the author experienced severe pain in their big toe due to the forgotten toenail clipping, causing them to take baby steps and feel sick. The pain lasted until they reached the bottom of the mountain, and the nail on their big toe turned black.

Semi obligatory to say that this did not happen today, but this was basically the earliest i could make this.
So i'm in my first year of college and was getting into the typical college stuff; partying, sports, alcohol, and of course academics.
About 3 weeks ago i was working on a math assignment online, which provides instant feedback on whether you got the question correct.
Typically its pretty easy and i'm done within about 30 minutes, but this one was incredibly difficult.
Already about 90 minutes in and not even halfway done, i had spent about the last 10 on one problem.
Confident in the answer i got, i submitted and saw that i was wrong.
Frustrated, i quickly (and according to my roommates, not even that hard) hit my laptop and went to see where i could have gone in the process.
I then wanted to change tabs, but for some reason my computer was not responding, which to me wasn't a big deal since it had happened a few times earlier, so i did what i normally did and did a hard power off.
Turning on the power again, my heart immediately dropped.
Black screen.
Computer beeping.
Message with something similar to 'error in bootup.'
I immediately check my phone on the error and see that it likely has something to do with hard drive, and it was confirmed on one of the info in the settings said that no hard drive was found.
Luckily my roommates were super nice and let me use one of their laptops to complete the assignment.
The next day i took it to the campus tech services for help.
And it took them about half a week for them to tell me that they wouldn't be able to help with the issue i originally told them about.
(looking back it was probably dumb to take it to them, since they aren't the biggest tech experts, but i'm a student and i'm not made of money.)
The next week was pretty bad, i spent it in the library or on the roommates laptops doing homework and searching on my phone for places to go to get it repaired.
And with my schedule conflicting with their open times (the only places that were open on weekends were way too expensive for my budget) and the fact that i didn't take a car to college and had to bum rides from one of my roommates, i was out of luck for that entire week.
Finally, late last week i finally got time to go to a repair place and finally get it done.
Upon immediate review the hard drive was busted and basically unsalvagable and i had to get a new one.
Luckily the people were kind and gave me a fair estimate of about $200 (which was like 1/2 other places were estimating) and also tacked on a student discount.
Still shipping for a new hard drive and repairs took a week, so that was another week in the library and borrowing laptops again.
Finally today i got news of it being repaired.
Spent most of the day reinstalling things and finally can get back to my usual daily life of web browsing reddit and steam games.
Math homework has also been a lot easier so the same thing repeating should hopefully be avoided for a long time now.
summary: A college student's laptop hard drive fails, causing problems with completing homework assignments and accessing important files. The student takes it to campus tech services, but they are unable to help. The student spends several days in the library and borrowing laptops from roommates to complete assignments and find a repair place. The repair takes a week, and the student finally gets news of it being repaired today.

So i'm in my first year of college and was getting into the typical college stuff; partying, sports, alcohol, and of course academics.
About 3 weeks ago i was working on a math assignment online, which provides instant feedback on whether you got the question correct.
Typically its pretty easy and i'm done within about 30 minutes, but this one was incredibly difficult.
Already about 90 minutes in and not even halfway done, i had spent about the last 10 on one problem.
Confident in the answer i got, i submitted and saw that i was wrong.
Frustrated, i quickly (and according to my roommates, not even that hard) hit my laptop and went to see where i could have gone in the process.
I then wanted to change tabs, but for some reason my computer was not responding, which to me wasn't a big deal since it had happened a few times earlier, so i did what i normally did and did a hard power off.
Turning on the power again, my heart immediately dropped.
Black screen.
Computer beeping.
Message with something similar to 'error in bootup.'
I immediately check my phone on the error and see that it likely has something to do with hard drive, and it was confirmed on one of the info in the settings said that no hard drive was found.
Luckily my roommates were super nice and let me use one of their laptops to complete the assignment.
The next day i took it to the campus tech services for help.
And it took them about half a week for them to tell me that they wouldn't be able to help with the issue i originally told them about.
(looking back it was probably dumb to take it to them, since they aren't the biggest tech experts, but i'm a student and i'm not made of money.)
The next week was pretty bad, i spent it in the library or on the roommates laptops doing homework and searching on my phone for places to go to get it repaired.
And with my schedule conflicting with their open times (the only places that were open on weekends were way too expensive for my budget) and the fact that i didn't take a car to college and had to bum rides from one of my roommates, i was out of luck for that entire week.
Finally, late last week i finally got time to go to a repair place and finally get it done.
Upon immediate review the hard drive was busted and basically unsalvagable and i had to get a new one.
Luckily the people were kind and gave me a fair estimate of about $200 (which was like 1/2 other places were estimating) and also tacked on a student discount.
Still shipping for a new hard drive and repairs took a week, so that was another week in the library and borrowing laptops again.
Finally today i got news of it being repaired.
Spent most of the day reinstalling things and finally can get back to my usual daily life of web browsing reddit and steam games.
Math homework has also been a lot easier so the same thing repeating should hopefully be avoided for a long time now.

The student takes it to campus tech services, but they are unable to help. The student spends several days in the library and borrowing laptops from roommates to complete assignments and find a repair place. The repair takes a week, and the student finally gets news of it being repaired today.

This fuckup is currently ongoing, as i'm in a burning pain.
About a week ago i felt like my earrings were pretty disgusting so i switched them out with another pair.
Being a dude who hasn't really worn earrings much in the past i've tried cleaning them a bunch of times but they never quite got the clean i wanted them to be.
I figured i'd look into some ways to clean them and after reading something (not really sure where) i settled on peroxide.
My plan was to leave them in the peroxide overnight and then clean them and see how they were in the morning... so i got a yellow plastic disposable cup and then put them in a bit of peroxide and let it go to see in the morning.... i forgot about them for quite a while and tonight, over a week later i decided it was time to take them out.
Being that the peroxide has been exposed to light i didn't expect much so i kind of just dumped it out and picked up the earrings... without rinsing them.
Now the gauge looks slightly bigger than my replacements so i decided to put one in to see if it fit still, and it did, you'd think that'd be the end of it right?
Wrong.
I put them on the counter and go to bed, about 5 minutes later i feel a burning sensation on my nose.... my hand... my ear?
Seeing as how i've had a traumatic week i'm not too worried about it, i feel like i'm just paranoid, so i get up just to check at a leisurely pace and turn on the light.... to see the tip of my nose, and a bit of both my hands bleaching quickly.
Quickly i begin flushing my skin with water and called poison control, who simply suggested keep doing as i have been.
So now part of my skin is mildly bleached, i'm throbbing in pain, and i can't fall asleep.
Fuck.

Context: i've recently come down with a pretty nasty ear infection, that just seems to get worse.
On the first day, my inner ear felt congested, and flared up in pain when i bit down on anything.
Obviously, i decide to head to a clinic, and was promptly diagnosed with an inner ear infection.
On the second day, i felt lightheaded and dizzy, but decided to push on through.
However, by the third day, i was starting to feel queasy, and heavily feverish.
I checked my temp with an oral thermometer, and, just as i suspected, i was running a low fever.
Now, here's where the tifu starts.
A couple weeks back, i made plans with a friend to go see justice league.
We were both pretty hyped up, because we're pretty big fans of the characters.
Even though i was feeling pretty shitty, i decided to go through with our  plans, and go anyways.
I had started to feel a little better by the time noon rolled around, so i thought i could keep it together until i got back home.
Boy, was i wrong.
When we got to the theater, my fever had slowly started to return, along with a stomach ache.
It started out pretty mild, but slowly progressed.
By the midway point, i was barely keeping it together.
Around the setup to the climax, i could feel my throat burning, and my stomach rumbling like a geyser, preparing to erupt.
And erupt it did... as i was starting to get ready to make a break for the bathroom, the inevitable time bomb that was my gut finally exploded.
Thanks to the advice i'd gotten about staying hydrated, the nearly-endless stream of vomit that shot out of my mouth was extra liquidy, leading to an ever growing puddle of puke, swelling up around my shoes.
Quickly, the soupy stream of spew made it's way down the isle, alerting everyone that hadn't already noticed the atrocity i had just committed before them.
Soon came an endless torrent of remarks, such as "geez, why's it all wet here?
", "who just spilled their drink?"
"why is my shoe so moist?"
And many more.
Eventually, the ushers had become aware of the mess i had  just jettisoned from my throat, and started evacuating the theater.
I couldn't make eye contact with my friend, as i rushed back to my car to speed home.

The person was embarrassed and couldn't make eye contact with their friend.

It's my wife's birthday in 2 weeks so i decided to buy her something really nice.
Yesterday while she was out on an errand i snuck out and bought a very expensive cartier item, making it back home before she got back.
This morning she wakes me up and shows me her phone with a worried look on her face.
On it there's a message from her bank warning her that a very large purchase was made on her credit card.
I jump out of bed, yelling "what the fuck!"
And grab my wallet, finding inside my wife's, identical to my own, credit card rather than my card.
The night before we went to dinner and must have switched our cards after paying.
Kinda shocked that cartier didn't bother to check the name on the card as we have completely different names.
summary: A man bought his wife an expensive Cartier item for her birthday, but when she received a message from her bank about a large purchase on her credit card, he realized they had accidentally switched cards during dinner the night before.

Yesterday while she was out on an errand i snuck out and bought a very expensive cartier item, making it back home before she got back.
This morning she wakes me up and shows me her phone with a worried look on her face.
On it there's a message from her bank warning her that a very large purchase was made on her credit card.
I jump out of bed, yelling "what the fuck!"
And grab my wallet, finding inside my wife's, identical to my own, credit card rather than my card.
The night before we went to dinner and must have switched our cards after paying.
Kinda shocked that cartier didn't bother to check the name on the card as we have completely different names.
summary: A man bought his wife an expensive Cartier item for her birthday, but when she received a message from her bank about a large purchase on her credit card, he realized they had accidentally switched cards during dinner the night before.

This story actually happened a good few years ago.
When i was younger my friends shelby and chris were over at my house.
We were playing around, and acting a fool like normal barely teenage kids would do.
Well at some point i go in the garage, and their standing outside at the garage door.
We're laughing and making faces through the windows of the door when i decide to jokingly charge at it making a weird face and some strange silent hill level movements.
Basically i stop too late, and end up hitting the garage door and the glass pane breaks with them outside.
I get cut up a bit on my arms from the glass, and shelby originally standing merrily outside is on the ground with a chunk of her skin cut off by a chunk of glass that shot out.
summary: Narrator recalls an incident from their childhood where they and their friends accidentally injured themselves by playing around and acting silly.

This happened in the past.
My co-workers and i decided to go out for some beers and thursday night karaoke at a nearby bar on a hot september evening.
Every one was having a good time, drinking beers, eating pizza and getting loud.
A song had been stuck in my head for days and by god i was going to get it out through the power of karaoke.
I submitted my song to the dj and waited patiently through some truly horrendous versions of the b-52s, journey and the usual karaoke suspects.
Finally my name was called, and after several bars of power chords, i began to sing a pitch perfect version of rock you like a hurricane by the scorpions.
I was nailing it; i mean i was on fire and i was feeling it but when i looked out into the audience there was nothing but shaking heads and even some looks of anger.
What the hell was going on i thought.
And suddenly just as the second verse started i realized what i'd done.
You see the date of this thursday karaoke night was sept. 1, 2005, and the reason that song was stuck in my head was that hurricane katrina had been in the news all week.
I never even associated the two things, but the audience clearly thought i was trying to make a mockery of the event.
Why hadn't my friends stopped me?
Maybe they were drunk.
Why hadn't the karaoke dj stopped me?
Maybe he thought i deserved the ass kicking that i was clearly asking for.
I weakly finished the song, dropped some cash on the table, and slunk out the door never to return.
summary: The author recounts a past event when he and his coworkers decided to enjoy a night of karaoke at a local bar. Their evening of fun turned sour when the author unknowingly submitted and sang "Rock you Like a Hurricane" by the Scorpions on the evening of September 1, 2005, coinciding with intense news coverage of Hurricane Katrina. The author, without realizing the connection until mid-performance, was met with an upset audience who thought he was making fun of the recent devastating event. After finishing his song, he quickly departed, vowing never to return.

When you think of a laboratory you wouldn't usually think of cheering crowds or actors in costumes.
You might not associate academic analysis with raucous outdoor performances or atmospheric indoor shows under candlelight.
But shakespeare's globe on london's bankside is a kind of living laboratory, with its own team of in-house scholars, researchers and academic advisers.
Everything from the physical design of the theatre through to the individual performances is informed by the insights and research work of academics the globe's site beside the river thames now has two theatres, with the opening of an indoor jacobean theatre alongside the existing thatch-roofed, open-air playhouse.
Building this much smaller, enclosed theatre, called the sam wanamaker playhouse, was an academic challenge in itself.
Farah karim-cooper, one of the globe's resident scholars, says that it's not a replica of a specific playhouse of the era, but a building assembled from different pieces of architectural evidence and contemporary sources.
The design, a wooden candle-lit chamber, with some of the audience practically on stage, is the result of "informed, rigorous speculation, based on all the available evidence".
But this doesn't mean an obsessive interest in re-creating "authenticity", says dr karim-cooper.
The buildings, like the performances, are about a living, breathing engagement with modern audiences.
"we're not interested in re-enactment," she says.
But she considers the theatre an experiment in seeing how things work in practice.
Like how do you move a play from the operatic scale of outdoor theatre to the close-up intimacy of the indoor theatre?
It was something that happened regularly in shakespeare's day, taking plays from the outdoor globe to an indoor playhouse such as the blackfriars, built in the atmospheric ruins of a monastery on the other side of the river thames.
It must have been like a rock band switching from a festival stage to a nightclub.
The globe was playing in daylight to open-air crowds, while the indoor theatre was a smaller, much wealthier audience, watching close-up in candlelight.
The globe team researched different types of candles, with beeswax chosen over tallow for the warmth of the light.
And in terms of lighting effects, the indoor theatre has pulley-operated candelabra - or else the actors themselves carry candles.
Light and darkness were almost characters in their own right in plays of this pre-electric era.
"darkness was a terrifying presence," says dr karim-cooper.
"darkness was palpable, something that people seemed to be able to touch, it was so thick.
It was very much associated with all the horrors of the imagination, the devil, demons, witchcraft -  that dark, dark world they felt was out there."
She says that if elizabethans or jacobeans travelled in time to modern london "their retinas would burn if they saw our levels of light".
Another big difference is that shakespeare's audiences would have been in the same lighting level as the actors on stage.
The modern experience of an audience sitting in the dark while the stage is illuminated - a convention carried into the cinema - would have been completely unknown.
In the indoor theatres, audiences were paying high prices to see and be seen.
The really big spenders could sit in seats at the side of the stage, where they expected to be as much part of the spectacle as the actors.
And one of the most distinctive features of plays at the reconstructed globe is that it's impossible not to watch the audience as much as the play.
"it was a very social occasion," says dr karim-cooper, describing the shakespearean-era theatre as a long day out, with little precise time-keeping and much comment on who was in the crowd and the finery of what they were wearing.
"contemporary accounts are more about the audience and who was there and what happened - more than the actual play," she says.
Putting the actors and audience in clear view of one another changes how plays would have been performed.
For instance, the great soliloquies in the tragedies become a conversation with the audience, says dr karim-cooper.
Modern audiences, in a darkened auditorium, might expect these classic speeches to be a form of introspective, interior monologue.
When the audience and actors are looking into each other's eyes, it becomes a different moment.
There are other big changes between a modern and shakespearean theatre visit.
It would have smelled very different, says dr karim-cooper.
There would have been a heady mix of the perfumes that were highly prized, alongside the earthy scent of thousands of people crammed in together.
Another sensory difference would have been the "soundscape", she says.
It would have been a much softer sound, as elizabethan london didn't have engines or loud machinery or amplified music.
"in terms of how loud things can get, they had no idea," she says.
"there are accounts of people being freaked out by the audience clapping in a playhouse, the sound was so overwhelming.
They never heard a plane taking off."
The language would have sounded unusual too.
The accent of the time would have meant words such as "move" and "love" would have sounded much closer to rhyming.
And the globe has been presenting readings of plays with the original pronunciation.
The role of the theatre's research team isn't to be trainspotters in historical accuracy but to provide practical advice for actors and directors.
"there is nothing worse than an academic who has never been on a stage, saying this is what you should do.
It wouldn't work," says dr karim-cooper.
Instead they talk to the performers about the plays and can research any detailed questions.
They pride themselves on a quick turnaround, going to the original sources and delivering an authoritative report within a few days.
"we want to get beyond wikipedia," she says.
She is co-editor of moving shakespeare indoors, a collection of essays on indoor jacobean theatres, and education is a key part of the globe's work.
There is a postgraduate degree course in shakespeare studies with king's college, london.
There are outreach projects with local schools and training events for teachers.
Every year there is a landmark schools production, the playing shakespeare series, with thousands of free tickets for london pupils.
It's been a huge success, with many  coming to see shakespeare plays who have never been inside a theatre before.
Dr karim-cooper says they want to extend the idea of the theatre as a laboratory.
"we want to become a research hub.
We want students to be here."
The "unique blend" will be the dramatic experimentation alongside the "literary rigour".
"we don't separate the practical from the academic."

The theatre's research team, led by Farah Karim-Cooper, provides insights and advice to actors and directors, drawing from historical evidence and contemporary sources. The team also works with local schools and offers a postgraduate degree course in Shakespeare Studies. The theatre's indoor Jacobean theatre, the Sam Wanamaker Playhouse, presents plays in a candlelit setting, with the audience practically on stage, creating an intimate and immersive experience.

Mining giant rio tinto has lowered its minimum acceptances target slightly in a last ditch effort to takeover south africa's riversdale mining.
Rio's offer of 16.50 australian dollars ($16.42; â£10.14) is now conditional on 47% of shareholders accepting it by 6 april.
Previously its minimum target was 50%.
The move came after talks on the a$3.9bn offer between rio and riversdale major shareholder, brazil's csn.
If it fails to reach the new threshold, rio tinto will pay riversdale shareholders only a$16 a share.
So far only 41% have said yes.
The other key shareholder in riversdale is tata steel of india, which recently increased its stake to 27% and also has a director on the company's board.
Csn, brazil's largest steelmaker, has also increased its riversdale stake to 19.9%.
summary: Rio Tinto has reduced its minimum acceptance target to 47% from 50% in its efforts to acquire Riversdale Mining. The company has offered $16.50 Australian dollars per share, but if the new threshold is not met, it will only pay $16 per share. So far, 41% of shareholders have accepted the offer. Key shareholders in Riversdale include CSN and Tata Steel, who have increased their stakes in the company.

I have a classmate who is really interested in guns, knives, explosives etc., we'll call him a. many weeks back, i took back some magnesium powder from the school lab for campfire effects.
A saw me placing it inside my locker, and offered to trade a spoonful of magnesium for a handmade firecracker explosive.
I agreed, as it sounded pretty awesome.
It looked like a cherry bomb but it was really small.
He told me that all i had to do was to light up the fuse and wait for it to explode.
Today i attempted to detonate it in class.
That was the first mistake because its an enclosed classroom.
Everyone else was at other lessons so it was empty.
Moving the tables to the side, i created a space where it could "safely detonate".
Lighting it, i ran to the back of class and took cover.
The fuse was a sparkler and it burnt all the way till the flash powder, but nothing happened.
I took out the fuse and realized that the portion of it inside the flash powder had already disintegrated.
This is the stupid part.
I didn't know what i was thinking.
Maybe i thought it was a dud or something.
I took my lighter and lit the rest of it.
My left hand (thumb, index and middle finger) was holding it when it exploded.
It was really loud and made me go partially deaf for the next 5 minutes.
My fingertips are heavily bruised and there is a bit of internal bleeding under my middle fingernail.
Right now i'm suffering from tinnitus in my left ear as i type with only my right hand.
My left hand is in a sock with ointment on it.
My only fear of this is that my hearing may be damaged and this could result in me not being able to go for a private pilot license course i plan to take up at the end of the year.
If anyone has shot guns without earplugs before, you may know what i'm going through now.
Do advise.
I didn't dare to tell my parents the truth, so i told them i smashed my fingers in the doorway.
For the hearing issue, i'm not sure how i'm gonna explain that.
P.s i think this is karma, because i drew a huge realistic penis on my friend's physics workbook yesterday.
Doesn't help that the 3 fingers injured form fleming's left hand rule.
Update: fingers and hearing pretty much back to normal, now i've paid the price of stupidity.
Now i think through everything many times before making a decision to avoid future fus.
Have a nice day.

Police in germany have charged a man suspected of being behind an attack on the borussia dortmund team bus.
Rather than having links to radical islamism, he was a market trader hoping to make money if the price of shares in the team fell, prosecutors say.
The suspect has been charged with attempted murder, triggering explosions and causing serious physical injury.
He has been  identified only as sergej w, and was staying in the team's hotel overlooking the scene of the attack.
Two people needed medical help after three bombs exploded near the bus.
Spanish footballer marc bartra underwent wrist surgery and a police officer was treated for shock.
Following the attack on 11 april, borussia dortmund's home champions league match against monaco was rescheduled a day later, which led dortmund fans to open their doors to stranded away supporters.
Police initially treated the blast as a terrorist attack.
However, the following week, investigators cast "significant doubt" on jihadist motivations being behind it.
They now say the attack was in fact motivated by financial greed.
Sergej w, 28, would have made about €3.9m euros ($4.2m; £3.2m) from his actions, germany's bild newspaper reported.
In a statement on friday (in german), the german federal prosecutor's office said he has german and russian nationality.
He was arrested on friday near tubingen in rottenburg, south-west germany.
The suspect had allegedly bought 15,000 put options on borussia dortmund shares - reportedly priced at €78,000 (£65,000; $83,600) - betting that they would drop sharply after the attack.
He would have made large profits if the team's share price collapsed.
Experts have likened the alleged plot to a sophisticated form of insider trading - because he tried to use information not widely available to the public to make money quickly.
He was staying at the team's l'arrivée hotel in dortmund on the day of the attack and had moved to a room on the top floor, overlooking the street where it took place, prosecutors say.
The suspect placed the bet on 11 april using an ip address traced to the hotel, after taking out a loan for the money.
Investigators believe three explosive devices packed with metal pins were hidden in a hedge and set off as the bus passed.
The bus was damaged about six miles from the westfalenstadion - officially called signal iduna park - in dortmund about 90 minutes before kick-off.
Pictures from the scene showed its windows broken and its tyres burst.

The 28-year-old, known as Sergej W, had reportedly bought shares in the team and betted on a fall in their value to pocket a hefty profit. Investigators suspect he was motivated by money after finding evidence of debt and financial problems, however, they say his motives were still unclear. His 15,000 put options reportedly brought in €3.9m in profits, but the suspects say this was simply an elaborate form of insider trading.

The suspect has been charged with attempted murder, triggering explosions and causing serious physical injury.
He has been  identified only as sergej w, and was staying in the team's hotel overlooking the scene of the attack.
Two people needed medical help after three bombs exploded near the bus.
Spanish footballer marc bartra underwent wrist surgery and a police officer was treated for shock.
Following the attack on 11 april, borussia dortmund's home champions league match against monaco was rescheduled a day later, which led dortmund fans to open their doors to stranded away supporters.
Police initially treated the blast as a terrorist attack.
However, the following week, investigators cast "significant doubt" on jihadist motivations being behind it.
They now say the attack was in fact motivated by financial greed.
Sergej w, 28, would have made about €3.9m euros ($4.2m; £3.2m) from his actions, germany's bild newspaper reported.
In a statement on friday (in german), the german federal prosecutor's office said he has german and russian nationality.
He was arrested on friday near tubingen in rottenburg, south-west germany.

He would have made large profits if the team's share price collapsed.
Experts have likened the alleged plot to a sophisticated form of insider trading - because he tried to use information not widely available to the public to make money quickly.

The suspect placed the bet on 11 april using an ip address traced to the hotel, after taking out a loan for the money.
Investigators believe three explosive devices packed with metal pins were hidden in a hedge and set off as the bus passed.
The bus was damaged about six miles from the westfalenstadion - officially called signal iduna park - in dortmund about 90 minutes before kick-off.
Pictures from the scene showed its windows broken and its tyres burst.

I work in a secure mental health hospital in the uk.
I typically work night shifts and last night i was getting peckish.
I thought to myself i'll pop some toast in and quickly go do my observations, by the time i'm back it will be ready.
As i'm doing my checks a couple of patients asked me to do some little things for them and i assist them, completely forgetting about my toast.
Next thing i know, the fire alarms are ringing.
See the interesting thing about secure door locks is that they become unlocked in the event of a fire, to allow people to get out the building, and well, the interesting thing about secure hospitals is that they are supposed to be locked... for the briefest of moments i was confused, then suddenly it dawned on me.
Toast.
I ran to the staff room (which, previously only accessible by staff,  was now open to all as the internal locks are released too) and found smoke billowing from the toaster and a patient sat next to it laughing and munching his way through the black charcoal blocks that remained of my snack.
Luckily, we managed to secure the building, reset the alarm and escort the patient back to his room with no harm done.
One patient however did manage to get out the building however and had to be picked up by police later in the night.
Lesson to self, no more toast on night shift.
Safe to say my manager was not impressed.
summary: A healthcare worker in a secure mental health hospital in the UK shared a story about how they forgot about their toast while doing patient observations and it ended up setting off the fire alarm. The worker had left the toast in the staff room, which became accessible to patients due to the fire alarm, and a patient found and ate it, causing smoke to billow from the toaster. Luckily, the situation was resolved without harm, but the worker's manager was not impressed. The worker learned a lesson about not bringing toast on night shifts.

Both me and my girlfriend participate in winter sports at our highschool, i swim and she fences.
Today was a late meet for me (8pm meet) and it is a rule we must dress up for a meet.
My girlfriend has a normal practice today, normally school gets out at 3:02 and her practice is at 3:15. she has to get changed so i wait outside the locker rooms for her so i could give her a kiss goodbye.
What i don''t realize is that my bus leaves while i''m standing outside the locker rooms.
Being a slow dresser she is in there till the last minute.
After she comes out i give her a kiss goodbye and walk outside.
There was nothing, nobody, but the steady snow fall.
Naturally i freak out and start making calls, my friend says he got dropped off already so i call my house... no answer.. my parents and older sister are working so no answer from them.. now i''m paying the price with a 6 mile walk hold in freezing temperatures in my thin dress shirt and no gloves or hat.
Wish me luck!
!
summary: I waited outside the locker rooms for my girlfriend while she changed, then walked out to find nobody.

This happened in the past.
My co-workers and i decided to go out for some beers and thursday night karaoke at a nearby bar on a hot september evening.
Every one was having a good time, drinking beers, eating pizza and getting loud.
A song had been stuck in my head for days and by god i was going to get it out through the power of karaoke.
I submitted my song to the dj and waited patiently through some truly horrendous versions of the b-52s, journey and the usual karaoke suspects.
Finally my name was called, and after several bars of power chords, i began to sing a pitch perfect version of rock you like a hurricane by the scorpions.
I was nailing it; i mean i was on fire and i was feeling it but when i looked out into the audience there was nothing but shaking heads and even some looks of anger.
What the hell was going on i thought.
And suddenly just as the second verse started i realized what i'd done.
You see the date of this thursday karaoke night was sept. 1, 2005, and the reason that song was stuck in my head was that hurricane katrina had been in the news all week.
I never even associated the two things, but the audience clearly thought i was trying to make a mockery of the event.
Why hadn't my friends stopped me?
Maybe they were drunk.
Why hadn't the karaoke dj stopped me?
Maybe he thought i deserved the ass kicking that i was clearly asking for.
I weakly finished the song, dropped some cash on the table, and slunk out the door never to return.

After some difficulty selecting a song, the protagonist's performance of 'Rock You Like a Hurricane' by Scorpions caused some audience anger. Unaware of the hurricane news that week, the protagonist continued to sing but was interrupted by some disapproval.

This happened earlier this week, but has only just culminated today.
Ages ago i bought tickets to a football (soccer) match on the online platform viagogo.
This is the home match for my clubs biggest derby, and it is massive.
A once in a lifetime opportunity for a fan from australia like me.
The ticket arrived at the address i specified - my mates place in london - 6 days before the event, no worries, i think, i'll just have him express post it to the hostel i'm staying at in germany!
Should be fine.
Except obviously it is now game day, and i have no ticket.
Turns out express post for letters isn't really a thing and they still can take up to a week even for such a close journey.
I wasted €190 on nothing, and have to spend the day not even 15 minutes from the stadium where i am missing the game of a lifetime.
summary: An Australian soccer fan purchased tickets online for a major game via online platform, Viagogo. With the tickets sent to his friend's place in London, he planned on having them express posted to his hostel in Germany. However, on the day of the game, he realized that the express post for letters could still take up to a week even for short distances. As a result, the fan missed his once-in-a-lifetime match despite being just 15 minutes away from the stadium, stating that the €190 spent on the tickets was a waste.

Ages ago i bought tickets to a football (soccer) match on the online platform viagogo.
This is the home match for my clubs biggest derby, and it is massive.
A once in a lifetime opportunity for a fan from australia like me.
The ticket arrived at the address i specified - my mates place in london - 6 days before the event, no worries, i think, i'll just have him express post it to the hostel i'm staying at in germany!
Should be fine.
Except obviously it is now game day, and i have no ticket.
Turns out express post for letters isn't really a thing and they still can take up to a week even for such a close journey.
I wasted €190 on nothing, and have to spend the day not even 15 minutes from the stadium where i am missing the game of a lifetime.
summary: An Australian soccer fan purchased tickets online for a major game via online platform, Viagogo. With the tickets sent to his friend's place in London, he planned on having them express posted to his hostel in Germany. However, on the day of the game, he realized that the express post for letters could still take up to a week even for short distances. As a result, the fan missed his once-in-a-lifetime match despite being just 15 minutes away from the stadium, stating that the €190 spent on the tickets was a waste.

One of the longest-held detainees at the us facility at guantanamo bay, a kuwaiti man, has been sent home, officials say.
Fawzi al-odah, 37, was released after a us review panel concluded he was not a "continuing significant threat".
He had been at the us facility in cuba since 2002 after his arrest in pakistan on suspicion of links to al-qaeda and the taliban - a charge he denies.
He had challenged america's right to detain him in the us supreme court.
Mr odah boarded a kuwaiti government plane on wednesday morning us time.
"there's no bitterness, there's no anger," his lawyer eric lewis was quoted as saying by the associated press news agency.
"there's just excitement and joy that he will be going home."
The release came after guantanamo's periodic review board in july determined "that continued law of war detention of (mr odah) does not remain necessary to protect against a continuing significant threat to the security of the united states".
But he now faces at least a year at a militant rehabilitation centre in kuwait, according to the terms of the release.
The kuwaiti government had pushed hard for the release of all kuwaiti detainees at guantanamo.
Mr odah had argued that he travelled to afghanistan and pakistan to teach the koran and provide humanitarian aid.
He is the first inmate to be freed since may, when five taliban detainees were exchanged for us sgt bowe bergdahl, who had been kept by the insurgents in afghanistan.
Mr odah's release brings down the total number of inmates at the us naval base to 148.
The us opened the facility in january 2002, following the 11 september 2001 attacks in america.
President barack obama has repeatedly promised to shut it down.

Mining giant rio tinto has lowered its minimum acceptances target slightly in a last ditch effort to takeover south africa's riversdale mining.
Rio's offer of 16.50 australian dollars ($16.42; â£10.14) is now conditional on 47% of shareholders accepting it by 6 april.
Previously its minimum target was 50%.
The move came after talks on the a$3.9bn offer between rio and riversdale major shareholder, brazil's csn.
If it fails to reach the new threshold, rio tinto will pay riversdale shareholders only a$16 a share.
So far only 41% have said yes.
The other key shareholder in riversdale is tata steel of india, which recently increased its stake to 27% and also has a director on the company's board.
Csn, brazil's largest steelmaker, has also increased its riversdale stake to 19.9%.

If Rio Tinto fails to secure the new acceptance target, the offer will be lowered to A$16 per share. Currently, 41% of shareholders have agreed to the deal. Brazil's CSN and India's Tata Steel are notable key shareholders, owning 19.9% and 27% of Riversdale respectively.

This happened a week or two ago.
I was in scotland with the main intention of climbing ben nevis, the highest mountain in the uk.
I woke up pretty early for this, and when i woke up realised my toenails needed cutting first.
But i was too tired, and the process of breakfast made me forget, and me and my dad set off.
There was little problem on the ascent, although i did realise that i'd forgotten about halfway up.
The walk down, however, was different.
After ten minutes of descent, with all of me feeling like shit from the climb, my big toe began to hurt.
Eventually it got to the point where i had to take baby steps to minimise the pain.
By the last half of the mountain every tiny step felt like i was stunning my toe.
Normally it's quicker when you go down a mountain compared to the climb, but my memory cost me hours and a shit ton of pain, by the end my legs were shaking and stiff, as i had to keep myself from moving too far with each step, using far more energy than i would have otherwise.
I felt sick and, after sitting down at the bottom, could barely bring myself to limp to the car park, since then the nail on my big toe has gone black, but the pain is gone.

The author notes that their memory lapse caused them to forget to cut their toenails before climbing, which contributed to the pain. The author also mentions that after the climb, their big toe nail turned black but the pain has subsided.

This fuckup is currently ongoing, as i'm in a burning pain.
About a week ago i felt like my earrings were pretty disgusting so i switched them out with another pair.
Being a dude who hasn't really worn earrings much in the past i've tried cleaning them a bunch of times but they never quite got the clean i wanted them to be.
I figured i'd look into some ways to clean them and after reading something (not really sure where) i settled on peroxide.
My plan was to leave them in the peroxide overnight and then clean them and see how they were in the morning... so i got a yellow plastic disposable cup and then put them in a bit of peroxide and let it go to see in the morning.... i forgot about them for quite a while and tonight, over a week later i decided it was time to take them out.
Being that the peroxide has been exposed to light i didn't expect much so i kind of just dumped it out and picked up the earrings... without rinsing them.
Now the gauge looks slightly bigger than my replacements so i decided to put one in to see if it fit still, and it did, you'd think that'd be the end of it right?
Wrong.
I put them on the counter and go to bed, about 5 minutes later i feel a burning sensation on my nose.... my hand... my ear?
Seeing as how i've had a traumatic week i'm not too worried about it, i feel like i'm just paranoid, so i get up just to check at a leisurely pace and turn on the light.... to see the tip of my nose, and a bit of both my hands bleaching quickly.
Quickly i begin flushing my skin with water and called poison control, who simply suggested keep doing as i have been.
So now part of my skin is mildly bleached, i'm throbbing in pain, and i can't fall asleep.
Fuck.
summary: The author made an error by cleaning his earrings with peroxide and inadvertently leaving them in the solution for over a week. When he removed them, he did not rinse them or the peroxide off his hands before going to bed.
